title: The Eddie Barefield union letter and the Cotton Club's $80 deal
summary: Thomas gets Barefield into Local 802 with a letter from a defunct union and explains the Cotton Club's deal with the union to pay eighty dollars a week.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Right. Well, see, I had to do the same thing for Eddie Barefield. Eddie Barefield... They was going to

make the whole band a travelling... Man, they called us up on the carpet. They were going to make the whole band... And that meant that the Cotton Club would have had to pay more money than that eighty dollars a week. They would have had to (?)put us(?) a traveling band to get more money.

So it just so happened that Eddie Barefield had that letter, and we took the letter down to the union -- and I went with him. Because Cab didn't have time to do all that shit. But see, I got to the place that he just let me run the band, and I ran it with the best of my knowledge. So I went down to the union, and I told them, I said, 'We've got this guy on the road and he's got this letter that says that he wants to be in the union, wherever he is...' He had never showed the letter before, see. He had never joined(?) ...(?)... And the letter was from a union. And he called them on the phone, and he said, 'Brothers, this union has gone defunct, so we'd happy for any other union to take him in.' And this other union, oh, man, they talked about that union like a dog! And that made it good for them. So they just automatically put him in 802. So that squashed it.
And see, the Cotton Club had something going with the union, too.

Because see, the scale for a job like we had was about a hundred and twenty some dollars a week. But by them giving us all this time, they worked a deal with the union... Because we kind of took the union up on it, when we found out that they okayed the deal. They made a deal to give us eighty dollars a week.
